newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria flights resume after aviation fuel crisis.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria flights resume after aviation fuel crisis.

text.p: Nigerian domestic flights resumed on Wednesday after they were paralysed by aviation fuel shortage, airline officials said.
"Our flights are operating normally," said an official of Bellview, one of the leading privately owned local airlines.
"The situation is back to normal," said an official at Kabo Airlines from the capital Abuja, adding "We are flying."
Flights were grounded nationwide on Tuesday by aviation fuel shortage caused by a dispute between state-run Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC) and the ports authority.
NNPC said in a statement on Wednesday that the dispute had been been resolved.

Ports officials stopped handling NNPC's fuel-laden vessels from the southeast and bound for the Lagos area because of a four billion naira ($50 million) debt owed the ports by the oil firm as handling charges, triggering the aviation fuel scarcity.
NNPC said it had made arrangements to transport aviation fuel to Lagos by road while it had also reached an agreement with the ports authorities on the debt.

Six vessels, including one loaded with 15 metric tonnes of aviation fuel, were expected to arrive in Lagos within days from the southeastern oil-producing city of Port Harcourt, the oil corporation said.

The port authority, which is also a federal government agency but which is expected to operate on a commercial basis, withdrew a credit facility granted to NNPC on ports charges to force the oil concern to pay up.
